_about: Humanity's space stations: every crewed orbital station flown, with the dates it was in orbit, its operator, mass, orbit and crews. Hand-compiled from Wikipedia and the NASA/Roscosmos/CMSA mission records; the live ones carry their NORAD catalogue number so the app can place them from CelesTrak elements, the past ones are placed on a schematic circular orbit (altitude and inclination real, phase not) when the map's date lies within their lifetime.

stations.first: the first space station; the Soyuz 11 crew lived aboard 23 days and died on re-entry when their capsule depressurised
the first military Almaz station, flown under the Salyut name; it depressurised and tumbled before any crew could launch
America's first station, built from a Saturn V third stage; three crews, 171 days, the Apollo Telescope Mount's solar observatory; it re-entered over Western Australia
a military Almaz with a reconnaissance camera and a self-defence cannon, test-fired once before deorbit
the civilian DOS-4 station with a solar telescope; two crews, 92 days
the last Almaz; two crews, 67 days
the first station with two docking ports, refuelled by Progress freighters; 16 crews including the first non-Soviet, non-American spacefarers (Interkosmos)
the last Salyut; it went dead in 1985 and was revived by the Soyuz T-13 crew in the most demanding repair of the era
the first modular station, assembled over ten years; permanently crewed 1989–1999, the 437-day flight of Valeri Polyakov, the Shuttle–Mir dockings; deorbited into the South Pacific
the largest structure ever assembled in orbit, 109 m across its truss, 16 pressurised modules; more than 270 people from 20+ countries have lived aboard
China's first orbital laboratory; Shenzhou 9 and 10 docked with it; an uncontrolled re-entry over the South Pacific
the second Chinese laboratory, visited by Shenzhou 11 for 30 days and refuelled by Tianzhou 1; a controlled deorbit
the Chinese Space Station: Tianhe core with the Wentian and Mengtian laboratories, T-shaped, three to six crew
